title: Token economics probe: sampled attribution pipeline for KV-cache-adjusted timings
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We need accurate per-token cost and latency attribution that accounts for KV-cache hits/misses without emitting prohibitively large telemetry volumes. Full per-token traces are expensive in storage and downstream compute. Goal: design and ship a sampled attribution probe that emits token-level timing deltas and cache-hit context for a fraction of requests, plus aggregated rollups for high-cardinality metrics, enabling cost accounting and hotspot dashboards while keeping telemetry cost under budget. This ticket covers schema design, sampling strategy, pipeline transforms, dashboard queries, and a gradual rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria:
- A telemetry event schema documented and approved that captures token emission latency delta, step type (generate/stream/prefetch), KV-cache hit/miss flag, model variant, sequence position, request id (sampled token-level id), and policy tags.
- Sampling strategy implemented: stratified sampling by model + latency bucket + customer tier with configurable sample rates.
- Ingestion transforms in the metrics/log pipeline to enrich events with route and cost coefficients and to produce daily aggregated rollups (per-model, per-route, per-customer) within storage targets.
- Example dashboards showing per-token median/p95 adjusted latency and cache-hit impact, and a cost allocation report that reconciles with billing within 2% for sampled workloads.
- End-to-end test demonstrating saved storage vs naive full-token emission baseline and no observable production latency regression.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions: 
1) Emit token probe events only for the first N tokens of a generation and for tail tokens beyond length thresholds to capture prefix vs continuation behavior.
2) Use reservoir + stratified sampling: reservoir per (model, region, customer-tier) with higher weight for enterprise routes.
3) Event size budget: limit additional fields; compress token-level timings into a small binary proto when possible.
4) To associate cache influence, emit KV-cache metadata: hit boolean, cache_key_shard, kv_latency_ms (nanoseconds resolution) and prefetch_hint flag.
5) Pipeline: ingestion -> dedupe -> enrichment (route lookup, cost coeff) -> windowed aggregation -> long term rollups. Use existing kinesis/topic and extend stream consumer to add join to route metadata.
6) Privacy: strip prompt text and only include hashed request identifiers.
telemetry_schema_snippet: event_type: token_probe | fields: {sampled_token_id, request_hash, model, model_variant, step_kind, token_index, token_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit, kv_latency_ns, backend_latency_ms, region, customer_tier, timestamp} - all primitive typed; token strings omitted
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): enable 0.1% reservoir sampling for internal customers + dev sandbox only. Monitor ingestion volume and dashboard correctness (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (gradual): increase to 1% for enterprise tiers and 0.5% for top-50 routes; enable aggregation jobs. (2-4 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): default sample rates 0.2% global with opt-in higher sampling for paid customers via console flag.
Fallbacks: if pipeline lag > 60s, auto-reduce sampling by factor of 10 and notify SRE.
